title: Query containment
objective: Decide containment of two conjunctive queries by a homomorphism, refute a claimed equivalence with a database instance once duplicates or NULLs enter, and stamp each method's result.

blocks.md:
Q1 is contained in Q2 when, on every database, every row Q1 returns Q2 returns too. Equivalence is containment both ways.

For select-project-join queries with equalities, under set semantics, Q1 is contained in Q2 exactly when some homomorphism maps Q2's body into Q1's and Q2's output variables onto Q1's. That is the result of Chandra and Merlin (STOC 1977), which lesson S9.L8 cites. Example: `Q1(x) :- shared(x, d), team(d, t)` and `Q2(x) :- shared(x, d)`. Mapping Q2's one atom onto Q1's first atom shows Q1 is contained in Q2: whoever has a share of a team's document has a share.

SQL returns bags, not sets, and a comparison with NULL is unknown, which WHERE treats like false, silently dropping the row {{run:RUN-pg-anomalies}}. A set-semantics proof can therefore fail for SQL. Refute it with an instance run in the tab on PGlite {{run:RUN-pglite}}.

A containment proof for the fragment under its stated semantics earns PROVED [P] of that encoding, uncertified. A distinguishing instance earns REFUTED [R], with the rows. "Results match" on one database earns only TESTED [T], with one instance {{run:RUN-pg-one-db}}.

Lesson S9.L8 compares a prover for a fragment, bounded checkers and refuters. None of them is taught here.

RUN-pg-anomalies.title: PostgreSQL 18.6: the isolation table of RESULTS.md (conditional UPDATE, read-modify-write, write skew, NULL, 22003)
verdict_lines: | Two concurrent `UPDATE acct SET bal = bal - 80 WHERE id=1 AND bal >= 80` from bal=100 | READ COMMITTED | both statements "ok"; second re-evaluates WHERE on the new row version (EvalPlanQual), updates 0 rows; final bal **20** — **no lost update** |
| App-level read-modify-write: both `SELECT bal` (100), both `UPDATE … SET bal = <read>-80` | READ COMMITTED | final bal **20**, but **160 spent from 100** — lost update / double spend |
| Same read-modify-write | REPEATABLE READ | second writer: **SerializationFailure, SQLSTATE 40001**; final 20 |
| Write skew: invariant sum(team) ≥ 0, each txn checks sum (200) then withdraws 150 from a *different* account | REPEATABLE READ | **both commit; team total −100** |
| Same write skew | SERIALIZABLE | t1 commits, t2 **40001**; total 50 |
| `UPDATE … SET bal = bal - 10 WHERE bal >= 10` over rows {NULL, 50} | — | only the non-NULL row updated; the NULL row is **silently skipped** |
| `9223372036854775807::bigint + 1` | — | **error 22003 "bigint out of range"** — Postgres raises, it does not wrap |
